title: Cacio e Pepe

ingredients.ingredient: Pasta (long noodles like spaghetti, linguine, or bucatini)

steps: Cook pasta according to directions. Meanwhile, crack a generous helping of black pepper onto a saucepan. Heat over medium-low heat for 3-5 minutes until fragrant. Add 2-3 small ladles of hot pasta water to the saucepan. Just before the pasta is done, remove the saucepan from heat. Conserve at least ½ cup of pasta water.

When the pasta reaches al dente, remove the pasta from the water and place directly into the pepper/water mixture. Working in small batches, add the pecorino to the pasta, stirring vigorously to create a creamy sauce. If the sauce gets too thick/dry, add a little of the conserved pasta water.

title: Grilled Herb-Crusted Rack of Lamb

ingredients.ingredient: ¼ tsp freshly ground black pepper

steps: In a small bowl, combine all the marinade ingredients (everything but the lamb). It should somewhat resemble a thick paste. Spread the marinade all over the rack of lamb. Cover and refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight.
Remove the lamb from the refrigerator and let it rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

Wrap bones in tin foil to protect against burning.  Use a two-zone setup. Start with two minutes on each side on high to create a sear before moving to the low heat zone.  Rotate and flip every few minutes until internal temp gets to 125˚. The fat tastes good, but if it's not removed be careful for flare ups.
It took about 30 minutes to grill two racks (a little under 1 lb each) the first time, but that could have been a mix of paranoia or poor temperature taking.
Let sit several minutes before serving.

title: Ultimate Shrimp & Grits

ingredients.ingredient: Cayenne pepper or hot sauce, to taste

ingredients.note: I used House Autrey Old Fashioned Stone Ground Yellow Plain Corn Meal
Original recipe called for 1.5 c. milk and 1.5 c. heavy cream

ingredients.ingredient: ½ lb. andouille or spicy Italian sausage, cut in chunks
1 lb. shrimp, peeled, deveined, tails removed
ingredients.note: I don't think I used a whole pound. I recommend 6-8 shrimp per person, depending on the size

ingredients.ingredient: 1 tbsp fresh flat-leaf parsley, finely chopped

steps: _Shrimp & Sausage:_

Place a deep, 12-inch skillet over medium heat and coat with olive oil. Add the white onion and garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes to soften. Make room in the pan and add the sausage. Cook until browned. The sausage should release a good amount of fat.

Push items to one side and tilt the pan in the opposite direction to gather the fat. Sprinkle the flour into the oil and stir with a wooden spoon to create a roux. Slowly pour in the chicken stock and continue to stir to avoid lumps. Mix everything in the pan all together. Toss in the bay leaves.

When the liquid comes to a simmer, add the shrimp. Poach the shrimp in the stock for 2-3 minutes, turning once. Shrimp should be pink on both sides and no longer translucent. Gravy should be smooth and thick.

Add a pinch of cayenne pepper or tabasco sauce if desired (be careful, a little goes a long way, especially if the sausage is spicy). Stir in the lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper, if desired. Stir in the parsley and green onions.
Serve over or beside the grits.
_For the Grits:_

Place a pot over medium-high heat. Add the half and half or milk and cream. Slowly stir in the cornmeal. When the grits begin to bubble, turn the heat down to medium low and simmer, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon. Cook for 10-15 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and thick.
Remove from heat and stir in the butter. Thin it out with a little extra cream or half and half. Season with salt and pepper, if desired.

title: Crab Quiche
footnotes: There was too much of the half-and-half mixture for the 9" round baking dish. Try using 2 cups of half-and-half and 2 eggs if using a 9" round dish.

ingredients.note: I use light
I use jumbo lump
See note at end
See note at end
or Gruyere or Emmentaler or a combination of any of the 3 cheeses

steps: _Prepare crust_
Unroll the dough. Arrange in a greased 9- to 9½-inch quiche dish or a 9-inch pie plate.  Seal all of the seams, tearing pieces to fill in the holes.
_Prepare filling_
Remove any cartilage from crabmeat.  Mix crab, bacon, and cornstarch.  Set aside.
In another bowl, beat together half-and-half, eggs, salt, nutmeg, and red pepper.  Set aside.
_Assemble and bake_
Place crabmeat mixture on crust.  Sprinkle with Swiss cheese.   Pour half-and-half mixture over all.  Drizzle with Topping ingredients.
Bake at 375° for ~40 minutes or until custard is set.  Let stand 10 minutes before cutting.
_Variation_
Can line a 9"x 13" dish with pastry.  Fill as above.  Bake at 375° for 20 – 30 minutes.  Cut into 15 appetizers.

title: Fall Harvest Butternut Squash
footnotes: If using candied nuts, add them to the pan after you season the apples and raisins.
I like to use a spritz of lemon juice and a garlic/herb mix

ingredients.ingredient: Butternut squash, peeled and chopped into large bite-size chunks

ingredients.note: I use ½ honey crisp, ½ granny smith

ingredients.ingredient: Spinach, kale, Swiss chard, or other sautéed greens

ingredients.note: I use spicy pork sausage

ingredients.ingredient: Olive oil, enough to coat squash
Lemon juice, garlic, pepper, or other seasonings for sautéed greens

steps: Preheat oven to 400˚ F. Place cut up squash into a large Ziploc bag. Pour olive oil over squash and toss to coat. Sprinkle with brown sugar and pumpkin pie spice and shake until well mixed and evenly coated on squash. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil, and spread squash in a single layer. Roast until roughly ⅔ cooked through, about 10-12 minutes.

While squash is in the oven, break up the sausage and brown in a skillet on the stove. Drain off the extra oil once browned. Meanwhile, chop the apples. Make sure you don’t chop them too small so they don’t disappear into nothingness when baked. Melt a sliver of butter in a large oven-safe skillet with lid. Stir in apples, pecans and raisins. Season with brown sugar and pumpkin pie spice, to taste.*

Remove the squash from the oven and carefully add it to the pan. Add the sausage and stir until well-mixed. Place lid over the pan and move it to the oven. Bake until squash is cooked through, about 5-8 minutes. When the squash is just about ready, sauté the greens. Lightly season to your liking*. When the squash is fully cooked, stir in the sautéed greens. May be used as an entrée or a side dish, with or without meat.

title: Acorn Squash Stuffed with Brandied Fruit

ingredients.ingredient: ½ cup brandy or wine (used apricot brandy)

steps: Cut squash in half and remove seeds and membranes.
Microwave on high, flesh side down, in ¼ cup water for approximately 8-10 minutes, or until tender.
Meanwhile, warm mixture of dried fruit and brandy in small saucepan.  Do not allow to boil.
Spoon half of dried fruit mixture into each squash half and serve immediately.
Serves 2-4, depending on size of squash.
_Notes_

I let the fruit absorb most of the brandy. When I stuffed the squash, I made some slits in the squash (could use a fork or knife) and "encouraged" the excess liquid to seep in. Original recipe said to stuff with a slotted spoon.

title: Cranberry Squash Bake

ingredients.ingredient: 1 cup apple or pear, cored and chopped but not peeled

steps: Cut squash in half lengthwise and remove seeds.
Place cut side down in baking dish and bake at 350° for 35 minutes.
Turn cut side back up.
Combine remaining ingredients and fill squash with mixture.
Bake 2 minutes more, or until squash is tender.

title: Apricot-Glazed Sweet Potatoes

ingredients.ingredient: ½ c. pecan halves (or chopped pecans)
1 12-oz. can apricot nectar or pineapple juice
1 c. light or dark brown sugar, packed

steps: Place apricots in medium saucepan and cover with nectar or juice and water.  Let stand 1 hour for fruit to soften.  Place over medium heat and simmer, uncovered, until apricots are very tender, about 30 minutes.  Cool and drain well, reserving liquid.

Scrub potatoes.  Place on baking sheet and bake at 400° for 40 minutes or until tender when pierced with a fork.  (Or you can microwave them until tender.)  Cool; peel and cut into lengthwise slices about ¼-inch thick.

Lightly grease a 2-quart (7" x 11") shallow baking dish.  Arrange half of the potatoes in a layer in dish, then cover with a layer of half of the apricots.  Sprinkle with half the brown sugar.  Repeat layers.
In a small bowl, mix ½ cup reserved apricot liquid (add extra nectar if not enough) with melted margarine, orange juice and rind.  Pour mixture over layers.
At this point, the casserole can be covered and refrigerated before being baked, for up to 2 or 3 days.  Before baking, bring to room temp.

Bake uncovered at 350° for 50 minutes, basting occasionally with liquid in bottom of dish.  (Basting may be difficult, so don’t worry about it if you can’t.)  Remove from oven and place pecans on top.  Return to oven and bake until casserole is bubbling and top is well glazed, 5-10 minutes.
Let stand 10 minutes before cutting into squares.

title: Asian Chicken Wings
steps: Combine and mix soy sauce, brown sugar and garlic cloves in a bowl.  Put wings in a single layer in a baking pan.  Pour mixture over chicken wings and marinate overnight.  Turn a few times during marinating.  Can also marinate in a plastic bag in a pan, turning it occasionally.
Bake at 350° for 1 to 1.25 hours until done.  Can baste once or twice during baking if you want.

title: Chocolate Babka

ingredients.ingredient: 1½ cups Nestle semi-sweet chocolate bits (used more—probably almost doubled)
3 heaping tablespoons plus 1 level tablespoon granulated sugar

steps: Place the flour, salt, and 3 heaping tablespoons of sugar in the bowl of a food processor fitted with the steel blade.  Pulse to blend.
Heat the milk to 120˚ (use a thermometer) and stir in 1 level tablespoon sugar and the yeast.  Allow to stand 7 minutes, until bubbly.
Cut the butter into tablespoon-sized pieces and add to the flour mixture in the food processor.  Pulse until crumbly.
Add the egg yolks and milk mixture and pulse until a ball is formed.  Remove the dough and place in a bowl.  Cover with a towel and refrigerate overnight.
Grease two 9-by-5-inch loaf pans.
Flour a wooden pastry board and rolling pin.  Divide the dough in half.  One half at a time, knead the dough and form into a circle.  Roll the dough out, forming two 22-inch by 18-inch rectangles.
In an electric mixer fitted with the whisk, beat the egg whites until soft peaks form.  Gradually add the ½ cup of sugar and the cinnamon.  Continue to beat until stiff peaks form.
Spread the dough with half the egg whites.  Sprinkle evenly with half the chocolate, the walnuts, and then sprinkle lightly with more cinnamon, if desired.

Turn in the outer edges of the dough rectangles and roll them up jellyroll-style.  Cut each roll into 8 sections.  Place the cut sections in 2 loaf pans, packing them next to each other with the cuts sides down and up.  Cover with a towel and allow to rise at room temperature for 2 hours. The dough should come up higher than the sides of the pan.
Preheat the oven to 350˚.  Bake the loaves for 35 to 40 minutes, until light brown.
Cool the babkas in the pans for about 5 minutes, then invert them onto serving plates.  Serve with the bottom side – the better-looking side – up.  Can drizzle with Chocolate Glaze (recipe below).
_Chocolate Glaze:_

In a small saucepan over low heat, blend chips, butter, and milk, stirring constantly until chips melt.  Remove from heat.  Stir in sugar until smooth.  Add additional milk if necessary for glazing consistency.  Spoon over cake.  Makes enough to glaze one loaf generously.

title: Bagels ‘N’ Lox Pizza
footnotes: If prepping in advance, stop here.  Cover and refrigerate.  To continue, remove from fridge and let sit for 30 minutes before finishing.

ingredients.ingredient: Fresh basil or other herb, chopped

steps: Press dough into a greased 10" x 15" x 1" pan.  Bake at temperature recommended on can for 8 minutes.  Remove from oven and cool.
Combine cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, Worcestershire sauce, and Tabasco in the bowl of a food processor and whiz for 30 seconds.
Place salmon all over pizza crust, tearing into pieces to fill.  Spread entire surface with cheese mixture.*  Sprinkle with tomatoes and herbs.
Bake at same temperature as before for 5 minutes.  Cut into squares and serve.  Makes 12-20 pieces.
Can also be served cold.
Cheese mixture can be made up to 4 days in advance and kept refrigerated.  Bring to room temp before using.

title: Baked Blueberry-Pecan French Toast
footnotes: I halved the recipe and used an 8" x 8" baking dish.  I used a Genuardi's baguette and used 16 one-inch slices to fit the dish.  I used extra blueberries to cover, about ¼ - ½ cup.

ingredients.ingredient: ½ tsp. freshly grated nutmeg (or ¼ tsp. ground nutmeg)
2 c. blueberries (about 12 oz.) or more (see note)

steps: Spray a 13" x 9" baking dish with cooking spray.  Cut 20 one-inch slices from baguette* and arrange in one layer in baking dish.
In a large bowl, whisk together eggs, milk, nutmeg, vanilla, and ¾ c. brown sugar and pour evenly over bread.
Chill, covered, until all liquid is absorbed by bread, at least 8 hours, and up to 1 day.  Turn bread over a few times during this period, being sure to moisten the crusts, to help the liquid absorb.
Melt 1 tsp. butter in a small pot.  Toss pecans in and coat completely, adding salt.

Preheat oven to 400°.  Sprinkle pecans and blueberries evenly over bread mixture.  Melt ½ stick of butter in a small saucepan with remaining ¼ c. brown sugar.  Drizzle over bread and bake 20 minutes, or until any liquid from blueberries is bubbling.

title: Baked Brie with Figs and Herbs
footnotes: Or you can score the edge with a sharp knife, wrap a long piece of dental floss around the cheese in the score, and then pull the ends of the floss to halve the cheese horizontally.

ingredients.ingredient: 1½ teaspoons minced fresh thyme (or ½ tsp. dried thyme)
2 ounces dried figs, preferably Calmyrna, coarsely sliced, about ⅓ cup

steps: In a bowl combine the first 5 ingredients.
With a serrated knife, cut Brie in half horizontally*. Place bottom half on large sheet of foil.
Press half of fig mixture onto bottom half of cheese; cover with top half of cheese.  Press remaining fig mixture onto top of cheese.
Bring edges of foil up around cheese; wrap.  Bake on oven rack at 425° until warm,  5-10 minutes (probably closer to 10).  Let stand 5 minutes.
Unwrap; transfer to serving platter.  Serve with crackers.

title: Baked Challah French Toast with Plums and Cherries

ingredients.ingredient: 4 tbsp. butter, cut in four pieces
1 cup pitted cherries, fresh, canned, or frozen (used fresh Bing cherries)

steps: Place the butter in a 9" square or 7" x 11" baking dish.  Microwave on high for 40 seconds, or until butter is melted.  Stir in the sugar and spread over bottom of dish.  Cover with the cherries and plums, and then sprinkle the orange rind over.  Arrange the challah over the fruit in one layer.  Set aside.
In a small bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, and vanilla.  Pour over challah, pressing down to soak.  Cover with plastic wrap.  Refrigerate 6 hours or overnight.
Bake at 350° for 35 minutes until puffed, golden-brown, and center is firm to touch.  Serve at once.  Spoon juices over toast.

title: Banana Chocolate Chip Cake

ingredients.ingredient: ¾ c. buttermilk or sour milk
ingredients.note: I make sour milk by putting 2¼ tsp. lemon juice in a measuring cup and adding enough milk to make ¾ c.  Stir and let stand 5 minutes before using.

steps: Grease and lightly four a 12" x 16" cake pan; set aside.

In a large mixing bowl stir together flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.  Add banana, butter, buttermilk or sour milk, eggs, and vanilla.  Beat with electric mixer on low to medium speed about 30 seconds or until combined.  Then beat on medium to high speed for 3 minutes.  Stir in mini chips.

Pour batter into prepared pan.  Bake in preheated 350° oven for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near center of cake comes out clean.  Cool cake in pan on a wire rack for 10 minutes.  Then remove cake from pan and cool completely on the rack.
Frost with chocolate or vanilla buttercream frosting.

title: Barbecued Fish with Maple Syrup, Chiles, and Lemon

ingredients.ingredient: 2 tbsp. minced red or green chiles, including seeds
¼ cup chopped cilantro sprigs, divided
4 6-oz. fillets of snapper, salmon, tilapia, catfish, or other fish*
ingredients.note: Marinade is enough for 3 lbs. of fish (8 servings)

steps: In a bowl, combine maple syrup, lemon juice, chiles, garlic, and 2 tbsp. of the cilantro and mix well.  (The marinade can be covered and refrigerated for up to 8 hours before using.)

Place the fish in a baking dish and rub the marinade into both sides.  Place in the refrigerator to marinate for 15 minutes.  Grill for about 5 minutes per side, depending on type and thickness of fish.  Sprinkle with the remaining 2 tbsp. cilantro and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Can boil remaining marinade and serve on the side.

title: Beets with Goat Cheese and Candied Walnuts
steps: Cut leaves and stems from the beets, leaving about a ½-inch stem.  Snap off the "tail."  Wash the beets; leave wet.  Place in a microwave-safe bowl. Cover and microwave on high about 12 minutes, until beets are tender.  May want to rotate the beets after 5 minutes so that beets at outer edge of dish are moved to the center.  Drain and cool.
In a small bowl, whisk together balsamic vinegar with sugar.
When beets are cool enough to handle, slip beet skins off with fingers.  You may want to wear thin rubber gloves.  Cut beets in half, then slice.
Pour vinegar mixture over beets and gently toss to coat.  Arrange on plates.  Crumble goat cheese over beets and sprinkle with crumbled candied walnuts.
Can accompany with greens.

title: Bellini Freeze
steps: Let peaches thaw slightly.
Combine peaches and orange juice in blender and blend until smooth.
Pour into large pitcher and slowly add champagne and club soda.  Stir gently.
Serve immediately.

title: Brie Baked in a Bread Bowl

ingredients.ingredient: 8 oz. cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces (used lite)

steps: Melt butter in large skillet and sauté onions and garlic until golden brown, ~10 minutes.  Melt Brie and cream cheese in microwave (used medium-high).  Whisk in onion mixture, sour cream, juice, sugar, Worcestershire, salt and pepper.
Cut off top of bread.  Scoop out bread center and reserve, leaving ¾" shell.  Spoon cheese mixture into bread bowl.  Top with bread lid, wrap in foil and place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 400° until cheese bubbles, 1 hour.
Unwrap; remove bread lid and sprinkle with paprika.
Serve with reserved bread chunks and/or cut fresh vegetables or crackers.

title: Brie Pinwheel
footnotes: If using chutney, you might want to add it right before serving so that it doesn’t stick to the plastic wrap.

ingredients.ingredient: Other nuts, fruits, herbs, seeds as desired

steps: Carefully cut away the rind from the top of the Brie.  Using the back of the knife, lightly mark the top of the Brie into equal wedge-shaped areas.  (For a 1-pound Brie, 6 sections.  For a 5-pound Brie, 10 sections.)

Sprinkle each of the ingredients onto one of the wedge-shaped areas and press gently into the surface of the Brie.*  Wrap and refrigerate.  Allow to stand at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before serving.  Serve with crackers.  (Especially good with Carr’s whole-wheat crackers.)
1-lb. Brie serves 8; 5-1b. Brie serves at least 20.
If using a 5-lb. Brie, use ½ cup of each topping ingredient.

title: Bumbleberry Crunch

ingredients.ingredient: 6 tbsp. unsalted butter, chilled, cut into 12 pieces

steps: _Filling:_ Combine the berries, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg in a mixing bowl.  Toss well to blend all the ingredients.  Pour the mixture into a 10" round baking dish.  (Used white oval quiche dish.)

_Topping:_ Combine the flour, sugar, and salt in a mixing bowl.  Work the butter into the flour mixture with your fingertips or a pastry blender (I used this) or 2 knives to form small pellets.  Cover the berries with this mixture.
Bake at 350° until the crust is light golden brown and the berries bubbly, 30 – 35 minutes.  Remove and allow to cool slightly before serving.  Can be served with ice cream or light cream.

This is quite sweet.  If you want to add more berries, especially if using a larger baking dish, I would recommend not increasing the amount of the other filling ingredients.  However, you should probably increase the amount of topping in proportion to the amount of berries.

title: Brussels Sprout Salad

ingredients.ingredient: ⅓ cup shredded or shaved Parmesan cheese (optional)
1 pound shaved or thinly sliced Brussels sprouts

steps: Whisk all dressing ingredients together. Toss shaved Brussels sprouts with dressing.  Add remaining ingredients.  Taste for salt and pepper.

title: Butterscotch Toffee Bars
steps: Melt butter over low heat or in a microwave.  Scrape into a medium bowl.  Stir in brown sugar.  With an electric mixer on medium speed, beat until well blended, about 2 minutes.  Beat in egg, then vanilla.
In a small bowl, stir together flour and salt.  Add to butter-sugar mixture.  Beat on low speed until dough is smooth, scraping down side of bowl frequently with a rubber spatula.
Stir in ½ cup Heath Bits.  Turn dough into a greased 9-inch square pan, leveling surface.  Sprinkle remaining bits over batter.
Bake 20-25 minutes at 350°, or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out with a few moist crumbs clinging to it.  Remove pan to a rack.  Let cool completely in pan before cutting.
This is very rich, so I cut it into 32 triangles.  Took 25 minutes to bake.

title: Broiled Salmon and Fruit with Pomegranate Glaze

ingredients.ingredient: 1 cup pomegranate syrup or pomegranate molasses
½ cup extra virgin olive oil
8-10 fresh apricots, pitted and sliced (~10 slices each), or 25 fresh figs, quartered, or a combination

steps: Combine the lemon zest, pomegranate syrup, olive oil, hot sauce, garlic, cumin, cilantro, and mint and stir well.  (This marinade can be covered and refrigerated for up to 8 hours before using.)

Position an oven rack 4 inches from the heating element.  Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil.  Place the salmon flat side down on the baking sheet and coat on all sides with one-third of the marinade.  Scatter the fruit around the fish and drizzle with half of the remaining marinade.  Turn the oven to broil.  Immediately place the salmon in the oven (close the oven door) and cook for about 5 minutes, until the fish and sauce begin to caramelize.  Turn the oven to bake at 300°.  Drizzle the remaining marinade over the fish and fruit and cook for about 5 minutes, until the fish is done.

title: Broiled Fish with Orange Sauce

ingredients.ingredient: 2 scallions, trimmed and thinly sliced (white and green parts)
4 skinless bluefish fillets (6 oz. each) or salmon, grouper or red snapper fillets (used salmon, with skin on)

steps: Using a zester, remove long strips of zest from the orange.  Set aside.  Extract the juice.  (There should be ½ cup of juice.)

Combine the orange juice, orange zest, soy sauce, honey, and sesame oil in a small pot.  Put over low heat until the marinade is just warmed through.  Remove from heat and stir in the garlic and scallions.  Let cool.
Put the marinade into a baking dish and add the fish fillets.  Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, but no longer than 2 hours.
Preheat the broiler.  Drain the fillets, pouring the marinade into a small saucepan.  Place the fillets in a baking pan lined with foil and broil 4½ inches from the heat until done, about 5 minutes.

Meanwhile, bring the marinade to a boil over medium-high heat.  Cook until the liquid is reduced by one-third, about 5 minutes.  Add the butter and stir until completely melted.  Remove the sauce from the heat and season to taste with black pepper.  Serve the fish fillets topped with the orange sauce.  Can garnish with orange segments.

title: Cheese Blintzes

ingredients.ingredient: 1½ cups cottage cheese, drained (used low-fat small curd)
½ cup sour cream (used low-fat) or thick yogurt
1 tsp. ground cinnamon, or to taste

steps: Combine cottage cheese, sour cream, sugar, and cinnamon.  Put about ¼ cup of the filling in the center of a crepe.  Fold the bottom third over the filling, then fold in the sides, then roll from the bottom up to create a package.  Repeat with remaining crepes and filling.

To bake, place in greased 9" x 13" dish.  Brush with melted butter or spray with cooking spray.  Sprinkle with cinnamon-sugar.  Bake at 400° for 15 minutes.  Serve immediately with favorite fruit topping.  (Used lemon curd and fresh strawberry sauce from Chocolate-Streusel French Toast recipe.)

title: Caramel Fudge Brownie Ice Cream Pie
footnotes: I left out the Caramel Sauce.  Instead, I used ¾ cup Chocolate Truffle Sauce on the bottom layer and the remaining sauce on the top layer.
If you use the Caramel Sauce, you will only need ½ cup of the Chocolate Truffle Sauce.  This recipe makes 2 cups.

ingredients.ingredient: 1⅓ cups semisweet chocolate chips or chopped semisweet chocolate
2¼ cups Oreo cookie crumbs (about 3⅓ cups Oreos)—can use low-fat Oreos
_Fudge Bars: (Need ½ of this recipe.  Freeze remaining bars for other use or eat them!)_
¼ lb. (1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into 8 pieces
1 tsp. instant decaffeinated coffee, dissolved in 1 tbsp. hot water
2 tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into 2 pieces
12 oz. semisweet chocolate chips or semisweet chocolate, chopped
2 pints each of 2 flavors of good quality ice cream, softened until spreadable but not melted (used Edy’s Espresso Chip for bottom layer and Double Vanilla for top)

steps: _Crust_

Combine the crumbs and the butter and stir until the crumbs are evenly moistened with the butter.  Transfer to a 9" springform pan.  Using your fingers, press the crumbs evenly over the bottom and 1" up the sides of the pan.  Check to see that the crust isn’t too thick where the sides and bottom of the pan meet at an angle.  Bake at 325° for 6 minutes.  Cool thoroughly.  Can freeze.  (Don’t need to thaw before using.)
_Fudge Bars_

Melt the chocolates, butter, and dissolved coffee in a double boiler, stirring until smooth.  Cool 5 minutes.  In a bowl, mix the eggs at medium speed for 10 seconds.  Add the sugar, salt, and vanilla and beat for 2 minutes, until the egg mixture thickens and is a light yellow color.  Decrease the speed to low and mix in the melted chocolate mixture.  Add the flour and mix just until no white streaks of flour remain.  Line an 8x8x2-inch  pan  with heavy aluminum foil, letting the foil extend over the ends of the pan.  Butter the foil.  Spread batter evenly in the pan.  Bake at 375° for 28 minutes.  They will look soft.  Cool 1 hour at room temp., then cover and refrigerate at least 5 hours or overnight.  Use the overhanging ends of foil to lift out of the pan.  Remove foil.  Cut half into ½" cubes.
_Caramel Sauce_

Heat the cream in a small saucepan and keep it hot, about 150°, without boiling it.  Put the sugar in a heavy-bottomed saucepan and cook over low heat until the sugar begins to melt.  Increase the heat to medium-high and cook until the sugar melts, caramelizes, and turns a golden color.  Watch carefully and stir with a wooden spoon occasionally to ensure it cooks evenly.  Remove from heat and slowly add the hot cream to the hot sugar.  The mixture will bubble up, so be careful.  Return the saucepan to medium heat and cook the mixture, stirring with the wooden spoon, until the caramel is completely dissolved and the sauce is smooth.  Cool about 30 minutes at room temp.  Can refrigerate up to 2 weeks or freeze.  To use the sauce, reheat it gently in a double boiler just until spreadable.
_Chocolate Truffle Sauce_

Put the cream and butter in a medium saucepan and heat over medium-low heat until the cream is hot and the butter is melted.  The mixture will form tiny bubbles and measure about 175°.  Do not let it boil.  Remove the pan from the heat.  Add the chocolate and let it melt in the hot cream mixture for about 30 seconds to soften.  Add vanilla and stir the sauce until it is smooth and all of the chocolate is melted. Can refrigerate up to 2 weeks or freeze.  To use the sauce, reheat it gently in a double boiler just until spreadable.
_Assemble the pie_

Spread one flavor of ice cream over the crust.  Sprinkle half the Fudge Bar pieces evenly over the ice cream.  Spoon ½ cup of Caramel Sauce over the Fudge Bar pieces.  Spoon ¼ cup of the Chocolate Truffle Sauce over the top, spooning the chocolate sauce in the spaces where there is no caramel sauce.*  Spread the other flavor of ice cream over the chocolate sauce.  Sprinkle the remaining Fudge Bar pieces evenly over the ice cream.  Drizzle the Fudge Bar pieces first with the remaining Chocolate Truffle Sauce then with the remaining Caramel Sauce.  Try to spoon the Caramel Sauce in the spaces where there is no chocolate sauce.*  Freeze the pie 15 minutes to firm the sauce.  Wrap tightly with plastic wrap, then with heavy aluminum foil, gently pressing the foil against the pie.  Freeze overnight or up to 2 weeks.  To serve, dip a dishtowel in hot water and wring out the water.  Hold the hot towel around the sides of the pan for 15 seconds.  Release the sides of he pan.  Soften at room temp. for about 10 minutes.  Use a large sharp knife to cut into wedges.  Serves 10-12 (or more—it’s very rich!).

title: Caramel Matzo Crunch
steps: Preheat oven to 375˚. Line one large or two small cookie sheets completely with foil. Cover the bottom of the sheet with parchment (on top of the foil). Do not skimp on this step! Line the cookie sheet with matzos, cutting extra pieces to fill all spaces.

In a heavy 3 quart pot, combine the butter and brown sugar. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly until it boils (2-4 minutes). Boil 3 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and pour over matzos covering completely.
Place in oven and immediately reduce heat to 350˚. Bake 15 minutes, but check every few minutes to make sure it is not burning. (You may have to reduce heat to 325˚.) Remove from oven.
If desired, sprinkle with ½ cup chocolate chips. Let stand 5 minutes, then spread them evenly.
While still warm, break into pieces. Chill in the pan in the freezer until set.

title: Caramelized Brie with Pecans
steps: Cover the top of a ripe Brie with light brown sugar, about ⅛" thick.  Arrange pecan halves decoratively to cover brown sugar.  Place on a cookie sheet or an oven proof serving dish. Bake at 350˚ for about 10 minutes.  (Watch carefully and remove from oven if cheese begins to run.)
Place under broiler one minute ata time until sugar begins to caramelize.  Watch carefully.  Do not let sugar burn.

If desired, you can put ½ - 1 cup of sugar in a heavy skillet and shake gently over high heat until caramelized.  Drizzle this over baked Brie.  Do not add water to sugar while it is cooking;  that can be dangerous.  Just let it cook until it becomes a light caramel color.
Serve with Carr's Croissant crackers and wheat meal biscuits.  Arrange crackers and red and green apple wedges around Brie.

title: Carrot and Chili Pepper Soup

ingredients.ingredient: 1 4-oz. can diced green chili peppers, undrained
1 cup light cream or half-and-half (used nonfat half-and-half)

steps: In a large saucepan (used 4-qt.) combine broth, carrots, onion, undrained chili peppers, chili powder, and cumin.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 12 minutes or until carrots are very tender.  (Took much longer.)

Place half of the mixture in a blender container or food processor bowl.  Cover and blend or process until smooth.  Repeat with remaining mixture.  Return all of the mixture to the saucepan.  Stir in cream; heat through.  Makes ~7 cups, or 8 side servings.

title: Carrot Tzimmes
steps: Peel carrots, yam, and apples and grate in food processor on grater.  Mix all fruits and vegetables.  Add sugar, matzo meal, salt, and nutmeg.  Coat 2-quart soufflé dish or casserole with margarine.  Pour half the remaining margarine into fruit and vegetable mixture.  Spoon mixture into prepared dish.
Combine ingredients for topping.  Spread topping over mixture.  Pour remaining margarine over top.  Bake at 350° for 1½ – 2 hours, covering with foil about halfway through so it doesn’t get too dark.
Can prepare a day ahead and refrigerate.  Then bake.

title: Chicken and Wild Rice Soup

ingredients.ingredient: ⅓ cup sliced leek or green onion

steps: In a large saucepan (used 4-quart) combine broth, carrot, celery, uncooked wild rice, leek, dried thyme, and pepper.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 50 minutes or until the rice is tender.

Meanwhile, melt butter; stir in flour.  Stir in half-and-half.  Cook and stir until thickened and bubbly.  Cook and stir for 1 minute more.  Slowly add half-and-half mixture to broth mixture, stirring constantly.  Stir in chicken and sherry; heat through.  If desired, garnish with carrot strips and fresh thyme.

title: Chicken with Lemon and Figs
footnotes: Made 2 batches.  Used ~4⅓ lbs. boneless chicken breasts in one batch and baked ~30 minutes.  Used ~6 lbs. boneless chicken thighs in other batch and baked ~40 minutes.

ingredients.ingredient: ¼ cup brown sugar, firmly packed
12 oz. dried figs, stems removed and cut in half

steps: Grease a large roasting pan.  (Used 9x13-inch baking dish.)  Combine juice, sugar, vinegar, and water.  Place figs and lemon slices in roasting pan and top with chicken pieces.  Pour vinegar mixture over chicken and sprinkle with pepper and 2 tbsp. parsley.
Bake at 400° for 50 minutes or until chicken is tender, basting frequently.
Place chicken, figs, and lemon slices on serving plate, top with sauce, and garnish with remaining parsley.

title: Chicken Breasts with Mushrooms

ingredients.ingredient: 3 boneless, skinless Empire chicken breasts, split

steps: In a blender or food processor fitted with a metal blade, pulse/chop the matzah meal, thyme salt and pepper until the meal is powdery. Place in a shallow dish, set aside.
In another shallow bowl, whisk egg whites until light in color.
Dip chicken breast pieces in egg whites, then dredge in matzah meal.
Place in lightly oiled baking dish (9x12); lightly spray one side of breasts with oil and place in 400˚ over for 3 minutes. Remove from oven and turn oven down to 350˚.
In a large skillet, sauté onions and garlic in olive oil until the onions are translucent. Add mushrooms and sauté for 3 minutes. With a slotted spoon, remove mushrooms and spoon over breasts.
With remaining juices still in the skillet, return the skillet to the flame, pour in sherry, stock, orange juice and paprika. Simmer for 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in parsley.
Pour sauce over mushrooms and chicken. Cover and bake for 45 minutes.
Garnish with more parsley and serve.

title: Grilled Chicken with Spicy Hoisin-Honey Sauce

ingredients.ingredient: 1-2 tbsp. finely chopped canned chipotle peppers in adobo sauce or 2 dried chipotle peppers (used dried red peppers)

steps: If using dried peppers, soak them in warm water 30 minutes; drain well and finely chop.
In small saucepan stir together peppers, hoisin sauce, honey, vinegar, mustard, and garlic.  Cook and stir over low heat until heated through.  Makes about 1 cup.
Brush on chicken pieces and grill until done.  Heat remaining sauce and serve on the side.
_Note:_ I halved recipe and used 8 boneless chicken thighs.  Grilled 5 minutes per side.

title: Grilled Chili Corn-Crusted Shrimp
footnotes: Made a salsa with pineapple, peaches, sweet onion, crystallized ginger, lime juice, powdered ginger and coriander and garlic.
This is also a good preparation for boneless chicken.  I baked thighs at 350° - 375° for ~15 - 20 minutes.
steps: _Make the glaze:_  Place all glaze ingredients in a small heavy saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until boiling.  Remove from the heat and set aside to cool.

_Make the corn crust:_  Place the cornbread in a food processor or blender and process until fine.  Add the cumin and paprika and process until just mixed.  Dump out onto a cookie sheet.  Bake 10 minutes at 350°; allow to cool, and place in a small bowl.
Thread the shrimp onto skewers and grill over a medium-hot fire for 2 minutes per side, or until almost cooked throughout.

Remove the shrimp form the fire, brush both sides with the glaze, and dip into the bowl of corn crust so that they are well covered.  Return the shrimp to the fire and toast briefly, about 15 seconds per side.  Serve with a fresh fruit salsa.**

title: Chocolate Bourbon Pecan-Pie Bars
steps: In a mixing bowl stir together flour, sugar, baking powder, and cinnamon.  Cut in the ½ cup butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.  Stir in pecans.  Press into bottom of an ungreased 13" x 9" x 2" baking pan.  Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a small saucepan combine the ¼ cup butter and chocolate; heat and stir over low heat until chocolate is melted.  In a small mixing bowl combine the eggs, brown sugar, bourbon or water, and vanilla.  Stir mixture until well blended; pour over crust.  Return to oven.  Bake 20 minutes more or until set.  Cool on wire rack.  Cut into bars.

title: Chocolate "Charoset"
steps: Chop raisins and almonds in a food processor.  Melt chocolate and butter in a double boiler.  Stir in raisins and almonds.  Drop by tablespoons onto wax paper.  Let sit at room temp or refrigerate to set up.

title: Cranberry Turtle Bars
footnotes: I had difficulty with this.  I also melted chocolate on the stove and drizzled it with a fork.

ingredients.ingredient: ½ c. packed light brown sugar
3 c. (12 oz.) pecans, toasted, cooled, then coarsely chopped
2 oz. (⅓ c.) bittersweet chocolate, very finely chopped (used chocolate chips)
1½ sticks (¾ c.) unsalted butter, cut into ½" cubes
1½ c. fresh or frozen cranberries (not thawed, if frozen), coarsely chopped

steps: _To make base:_ Line a 15" x 10" x1" baking pan with foil, leaving a 2" overhang on the 2 short sides.  Butter all 4 sides (but not the bottom).  Blend flour, brown sugar, and salt in food processor, then add butter and pulse until mixture begins to form small, pea-size lumps.  (Or you can do this by hand with a pastry blender.)  Sprinkle into baking pan, then press down firmly all over with a metal spatula (and/or fingers) to form an even layer.  Bake at 350° until golden and firm to the touch, 15-20 minutes.  Cool in pan on a rack.

_To make topping:_ Melt butter in a 3-qt. heavy saucepan over moderate heat and stir in sugar, corn syrup, and salt.  Boil over moderately high heat, stirring occasionally, until caramel registers 245° on candy thermometer, about 8 minutes.  Carefully stir in cranberries, then boil until caramel returns to 245°.  Remove from heat and stir in vanilla, then stir in pecans until well coated.  Working quickly, spread caramel topping over base, using a fork to distribute nuts and berries evenly.  Cool completely.

_To cut and decorate:_ Lift bars in foil from pan and transfer to cutting board.  Cut into bars.  Place chocolate in heavy-duty plastic sealable bag.  Microwave on high for 45 seconds; knead bag to mix.  Microwave at additional 10-second intervals, kneading until smooth.  Cut a small hole in bag’s corner; squeeze and drizzle over base.*
They freeze well.

title: Chocolate Pumpkin Brownies

ingredients.ingredient: ⅓ cup miniature semisweet chocolate pieces (used more—try ½ cup)

steps: In a large mixing bowl combine brown sugar, pumpkin, the whole egg, egg whites, and oil.  Beat with an electric mixer on medium speed until blended.  Add flour, baking powder, cocoa powder, cinnamon, allspice, salt, and nutmeg.  Beat on low speed until smooth.  Stir in semisweet chocolate pieces.

Spray an 11 x 7 x 1½-inch baking pan or an 8- or 9-inch-square baking pan with nonstick coating.  Pour batter into pan; spread evenly.  Bake at 350° for 15 minutes or until a wooden toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean.  Cool in pan on a wire rack.  Cut into 2-inch squares.

title: Chocolate Raspberry Cake a la Simca
footnotes: The chocolate layer cake was not all that special, considering the effort and expense.  I might use a denser, easier recipe instead

ingredients.note: I couldn’t get fresh raspberries, so I used a 12-oz. bag of sweetened frozen raspberries, thawed.  I eliminated the ⅓ cup of sugar.  The liquid leaked as the cake sat, so you might not want to put the excess juice on.

ingredients.ingredient: ½ cup crème de cassis, plus optional extra for thinning the icing

steps: Butter and flour a 9" round cake pan.  Line the bottom with waxed paper.  Butter and flour the waxed paper; shake to remove the excess.

Combine 8 oz. of the chocolate, 2 tbsp. of the espresso powder, and ¼ cup of the cassis in a heavy saucepan, and stir over low heat until the chocolate is melted.  Stir to blend the mixture.  Remove the pan from the heat and add the egg yolks one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Return the pan to the heat and cook, stirring, for 2 minutes.  Remove the pan from the heat once more and add the butter, beating it in 1 tbsp at a time.  Stir in the flour.
Combine the raspberries, ⅓ cup of the sugar, and 1 tbsp. of the cassis in a bowl.  Toss to combine, and set aside.

Combine the egg whites and the salt, and beat until they form soft peaks.  Sprinkle the remaining ⅓ cup sugar over the whites and beat until glossy, 30 seconds.  Fold the whites, in thirds, into the chocolate mixture.  Pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake at 375° until the cake is slightly puffed but not completely cooked in the center, 20 minutes.

Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 45 minutes.  Unmold it onto a plate, then flip it onto a serving platter.  Leaving a 1" border around the edges, scoop out the top ½" of cake.  Fill the cake with the reserved raspberries, patting them down gently.

Combine the remaining 8 oz. chocolate with the water, the remaining 1 tbsp. espresso powder, and the remaining 3 tbsp. cassis in a heavy saucepan.  Place over low heat and stir until melted and blended.  Remove the pan from the heat and glaze the cake while the icing is still warm.  Cover the top and the sides.  You can spread it on everything or on just the cake part; then thin the remaining icing with some cassis and drizzle it over the raspberries.

title: Chocolate Snowball Cake

ingredients.ingredient: 2⅔ c. semisweet chocolate chips (about a pound)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°.  Line a 10-cup ovenproof glass bowl smoothly with foil.  Spray foil with nonstick spray.
Combine dark rum and instant coffee in small bowl; stir to dissolve coffee.
Combine chocolate chips and butter in a large bowl.  Melt in a microwave oven, stirring until butter and chocolate are melted and smooth.
Using electric mixer, beat in sugar, then coffee mixture.  Beat until mixture cools to lukewarm.  Beat in eggs, one at a time.  Transfer batter to foil-lined bowl.

Bake cake until top is cracked and dry about one hour.  Cool cake in bowl on rack 15 minutes - center of cake will fall.  (This does not happen to Janet’s cake.)  Press edge of cake firmly to level with center of cake.  (Janet does not have to do this.)
Refrigerate cake (covered) for at least 6 hours and up to 2 days.  Invert bowl with cake onto cake platter. Lift off bowl; peel off foil.
_Whipped Topping:_ Beat cream in large bowl until peaks form.  Spread over cake.
_Chocolate Glaze:_ Follow instructions for glaze (and freezing, if desired) for Chocolate Truffle Cake.

title: Chocolate Toffee Crunch Bars

ingredients.ingredient: 1 cup white chocolate chips or ⅔ cup sliced almonds (I used some of each)

steps: In a large bowl, beat butter with an electric mixer or by hand until creamy.  Add brown sugar and egg yolk, beating until smooth.  Stir in flour and half of the toffee bits, mixing until well blended.
Press mixture firmly into ungreased 15" x 10"x 1" jelly-roll pan.  Bake at 350° until golden, about 15-18 minutes.

Remove from oven.  Immediately sprinkle semi-sweet chocolate chips on top.  Let stand 5 minutes, or until chips are softened.  Smooth evenly over top with a knife.  Sprinkle white chocolate chips or almonds and remaining toffee bits over chocolate.  Cool completely, then cut into bars.

title: Chocolate-Streusel French Toast

ingredients.ingredient: ⅓ cup brown sugar, firmly packed

steps: Combine eggs, buttermilk, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt and sugar.

Cut challah into ¾-inch thick diagonal slices.  Thoroughly soak in egg mixture and place on greased cookie sheets.  Cover and chill 1 hour.  Prepare Chocolate-Streusel Topping and Strawberry Sauce (see below).
Sprinkle streusel over each slice.  Bake at 350° for 18 – 20 minutes or until lightly brown.  Serve with Warm Strawberry Sauce.
_Chocolate-Streusel Topping:_ Combine flour, sugar and cinnamon.  Cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs.  Add chocolate chips.
_Warm Strawberry Sauce:_ Combine strawberries with sugar and let rest 1 hour.  Warm in microwave (~ 1 minute?) and serve.

title: Chocolate-Coconut Macaroon Tart
footnotes: The crust was meant for a 9” pie plate.  It would also work well in a 10” tart pan and perhaps a 9” tart pan.  If you use this crust in a recipe where you are not baking the filling, it is probably best to bake the crust until set, about 8 minutes. Cool before filling.

ingredients.ingredient: ½ c. dried cranberries or cherries
1 tbsp. unsalted butter, cut into 2 pieces
6 oz. semisweet chocolate chips or semisweet chocolate, chopped

steps: _For the Crust:_ Crush cookies with berries in food processor until both are finely ground.  Add butter and process to combine.  Press into bottom and up sides of an 11" tart pan*.  Chill.
_For the Filling:_
Put the egg whites in a clean large bowl and set aside.

Put the egg yolks in another large bowl and beat with the salt using an electric mixer just to break up the yolks.  Add 1¼ cups of the sugar and beat on medium speed about 1 minute, until the mixture thickens and lightens slightly in color.  Decrease the speed to low and stir in the coconut, cream, melted butter, lemon juice, vanilla, and almond extract.  Set aside.

Use clean dry beaters to beat the egg whites with the cream of tartar at low speed until the egg whites are foamy.  Increase the speed to medium-high and beat until soft peaks form.  Slowly add the remaining ¼ cup of sugar, 1 tablespoon at a time.  Fold about half of the egg white mixture into the coconut mixture, then fold in the remaining egg white mixture.

Pour the coconut filling into the tart crust.  The mixture will fill the pastry.  Place the pan on a baking sheet.  Bake at 375° for about 40 minutes until the top of the tart is golden and the center remains set if you give the tart a gentle shake.  Cool the tart thoroughly, about 1 hour at room temperature.  The center will sink slightly.

_For the glaze:_ Put the cream and butter in a medium saucepan and heat over medium-low heat until the cream is hot and the butter is melted.  The hot cream mixture will form tiny bubbles and measure about 175° on a food thermometer.  Do not let the mixture boil.  Remove the pan from the heat.  Add the chocolate and let it melt in the hot cream mixture for about 30 seconds to soften.  Add the vanilla and stir the sauce until it is smooth and all of the chocolate is melted.  Gently pour the glaze over the center of the cooled tart.  Using a thin spatula, spread the glaze over the tart, leaving a 1-inch border without glaze.

This tart freezes well.  Chill first to set the glaze.  Then remove from pan, slide onto a plate or cardboard cake circle, and wrap tightly with plastic wrap and then foil.  To serve, thaw overnight in frig.  Uncover and let it sit at room temperature 15 minutes before serving.  The glaze should soften slightly, but the filling should be cold.  (I did not freeze it.)

title: Bittersweet Chocolate Torte with Raspberries
footnotes: I used an 8½" springform pan and baked the cake for ~30 minutes.

ingredients.ingredient: 14 oz. bittersweet or semisweet chocolate, chopped
¼ c. seedless red raspberry jam

steps: Grease bottom only of an 8" heart-shaped pan with removable bottom or an 8" springform pan.*  Set aside.
Melt chocolate with margarine and milk in double boiler over hot water; cool for 20 minutes.
In large bowl beat eggs and vanilla with electric mixer on low speed until well combined.  Add sugar and flour.  Then beat on high speed for 10 minutes.  Stir chocolate mixture into egg mixture.

Spread batter evenly in prepared pan.  Then place in a shallow baking pan on oven rack.  Bake at 325° about 30 minutes or till cake is slightly puffed on outer ⅓ of the top.  (If using 8" springform pan, bake about 35 minutes.)

Remove heart-shaped or springform pan from baking pan.  Cool cake in pan on wire rack for 20 minutes.  Loosen cake from sides of pan, then remove sides of pan.  Cool for 2-3 hours more or until completely cooled.  Remove cake from bottom of pan.  Wrap cake in foil and chill in frig. 6-48 hours.  (Or freeze and put in frig. early in day you wish to serve it.)

Just before serving (or up to a few hours ahead), bring cake to room temp.  In small saucepan heat jam until melted; cool.  (If it gels again, melt again briefly until spreadable.)  Spread jam over top of cake.  Place raspberries, hole sides down, on top of entire jam layer.  You may wish to sprinkle top with confectioners’ sugar.  (If not serving immediately, chill till shortly before serving.)

title: Chutney Brush-On

ingredients.ingredient: Several dashes bottled hot pepper sauce

steps: In a small saucepan stir together all ingredients.  Cook and stir over medium heat until heated through.  Brush evenly onto poultry or meat during last 5 minutes of grilling.  Heat remaining brush-on until bubbly.  Pass with meat. Makes enough for 4 pounds of meat.

title: Citrus-Honey Marinade
steps: In a small bowl stir together all ingredients.  (A whisk helps.)  Pour over fish.  Turn to coat.  Marinate in refrigerator 1 hour, turning occasionally.  Drain fish, reserving marinade.  Grill fish until done, brushing with reserved marinade.  Can boil remaining marinade and spoon over.  Makes enough for 1½ lbs. fish (maybe 2 lbs.).  Also good on shrimp.  (Used 1½ lb. swordfish steaks and 4 jumbo shrimp to serve 4.  Used 1½ times recipe, but had too much leftover marinade.  Single recipe would have been fine.)

title: Claudia's Roasted Vegetables

ingredients.ingredient: 1 bunch asparagus (about 1 lb.), woody ends broken off
1 giant sweet onion (about 1 lb.), cut in chunks
1 large or 2 small yams or sweet potatoes (about ¾ lb.), peeled and cut in chunks
3-4 carrots, peeled and cut in 1" chunks on the diagonal
2-3 leeks (about ¾ lb.), washed well, leafy part removed, cut in half lengthwise
2 small or 1 large red peppers (about ¾ lb.), cut in chunks
½ lb. green beans, ends removed (or 1 pkg. haricot vert)

steps: Put all in very large shallow roasting pan.  (I used 11" x 16" x 2" pan.)  Coat all vegetables lightly with olive oil and sprinkle with pepper.  Roast, uncovered, at 375º to 400º for 1 to 1½ hours, tossing every 15 minutes and scraping bottom, until everything is browned.

title: Coconut Lemon Squares
steps: Mix crust ingredients together with a food processor or electric mixer.  Press in the bottom of an ungreased 9" x 13" pan.  Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.

For filling, combine eggs and brown sugar in a bowl.  Add coconut and mix well.  Stir in remaining ingredients and spread evenly over crust.  Bake for 25 minutes.  Cool and cut into bars.  Freezes well.
_Note:_  You can halve this recipe and bake in an 8" x 8" pan.  You might need to reduce the baking times slightly.

title: Coffee Chocolate Chip Coffee Cake

ingredients.ingredient: ¾ c. packed light brown sugar
4 tsp. instant decaf coffee granules, dissolved in 4 tsp. hot water

steps: Put flour, sugars, and cinnamon in a large mixing bowl.  Stir together.  Add oil and dissolved coffee and stir until flour is evenly moistened.  Mixture will be crumbly.  Put ½ cup of mixture in a small bowl and mix in ½ cup chocolate chips.  Set aside.

Put sour cream and egg in another small bowl and stir together.  Gently stir in baking powder and baking soda.  Add sour cream mixture to flour mixture and stir until batter is evenly moistened.  Stir in remaining 1 cup chocolate chips.

Spread batter evenly in greased 8" x 8" x 2" pan.  Sprinkle reserved crumb mixture evenly over batter.  Bake at 300° for 55 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in center of cake comes out clean.  Cool in pan on wire cooling rack until chocolate chips are firm, ~5 hours.  To speed cooling of chips in topping, refrigerate cake for 30 minutes. Freezes well.
Note:  If you are not freezing it, it might not matter so much that the chips become firm.

title: Corn and Cheese Enchiladas

ingredients.ingredient: 5 scallions, white and light green parts, chopped
1½ cups fresh corn kernels from 2 medium ears (used Trader Joe’s frozen supersweet organic corn kernels, thawed and wiped dry)

ingredients.note: Nonfat milk may not thicken.  I used 2 parts half-and-half, 1 part skim milk.

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Stack tortillas, wrap in foil and bake until softened, 8 to 10 minutes.

While tortillas are baking, oil a 7-by-11-inch glass baking dish.  Warm 1 Tbsp. oil in large skillet over medium-high heat.  Add scallions and garlic, and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.  Stir in corn and milk and cook, stirring occasionally, until thickened, 7 to 10 minutes.

Remove tortillas from foil.  Set aside ½ cup cheese.  Spoon a heaping tablespoon of corn mixture in center of a tortilla.  Sprinkle with a heaping tablespoon of cheese.  Roll up tortilla and set in dish, seam side down.  Repeat with remaining tortillas, overlapping them slightly.  Pour enchilada sauce over tortillas and sprinkle with reserved ½ cup cheese.  Bake until bubbling, about 20 minutes.
Note: I made 1½ times the recipe to make 12 enchiladas.  Baked in 9" x 13" baking dish.  Used 12 oz. bottle of Trader Joe’s enchilada sauce, ½ cup of half-and-half and ¼ cup of nonfat milk.

title: Crab, Brie, and Pear Strudel

ingredients.ingredient: 6 ounces Brie cheese, rind removed and cut into ¼-inch cubes
½ cup thinly sliced green onions
½ cup diced fully cooked ham (optional)
1 pkg. (17.3 ounces) Pepperidge Farm Puff Pastry Sheets, thawed
2½ cups finely chopped peeled ripe pears (used Comice—too juicy; try Bosc or another firm variety)

steps: In a large bowl, combine the first eight ingredients; set aside.

On a large sheet of parchment paper, draw a 12" x 16" rectangle.  Turn paper over.  Sprinkle some flour on the paper.  Unfold 1 pastry sheet on the paper.  Roll the pastry sheet into a 16 x 12-inch rectangle, using the drawn one as a guide.

With the short side facing you, spoon half the crab mixture lengthwise down the center of the pastry. Cut strips 2 inches apart from the 2 sides of the pastry to within ½ inch of the filling.  Starting at one end, fold the pastry strips over the filling, alternating sides, to cover the filling.  Repeat with the remaining pastry sheet and crabmeat mixture using another piece of paper.  Lift both strudels with parchment papers onto a 12" x 16" baking sheet.  Trim parchment paper.

Beat egg and water together.  Brush the pastries with the egg mixture. Bake at 375° for 35 minutes or until the pastries are golden brown.  Let the pastries cool on the baking sheet on a wire rack for 30 minutes.  Slice using a serrated knife.

title: Cranberry Bars

ingredients.ingredient: ¼ c. firmly packed dark brown sugar
1 tbsp. Grand Marnier (used Triple Sec or Sabra) or orange juice

steps: Mix butter, brown sugar, and ½ cup flour together with a food processor or electric mixer.  Press firmly into the bottom of an ungreased 8" x 8" pan.  Bake at 350° for 7 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine remaining 2 tbsp. flour with egg, granulated sugar, dried cranberries, pecans, coconut, Grand Marnier, orange zest, vanilla, and salt.  Stir well to mix.  Carefully spread over warm crust and return to oven.
Bake 20 – 25 minutes, until edges are lightly browned.  Remove pan to a rack and let cool completely before cutting into 25 bars.
_Variation:_
I doubled recipe and baked in 9" x 13" pan.  Baked crust ~9 minutes. Eliminated pecans.  Used 1 cup coconut, ~1¼ cups cranberries, ~1¼ cups combined chocolate chips and chunks.  Made 35 bars.

title: Cranberry Chocolate Oat Bars

ingredients.ingredient: ¾ cup butter or margarine, softened
½ cup chopped dried cranberries, divided

steps: Combine flour, oats, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a medium bowl; set aside.  Beat butter and brown sugar in a large bowl until creamy.  Add eggs, flour mixture, ½ cup chocolate chunks, and ¼ cup cranberries; blend well.
Spread batter into a 12" x 9" baking pan coated with cooking spray.  Sprinkle evenly with remaining chocolate chunks, cranberries and nuts.
Bake in a preheated 350° oven 28-32 minutes or until a deep golden brown.  Cut into squares.

title: Cranberry Chocolate Chip Coconut Macaroons
footnotes: The original recipe called for aluminum foil, but the cookies were very difficult to remove from the foil.  If you don’t have parchment paper, maybe try greasing the foil.
If you bake one sheet at a time, bake it on the lower rack.

ingredients.note: Can be made for Passover by substituting 5/8 cups of matzo cake flour for each cup of flour.

ingredients.ingredient: 10½ oz. (4 loosely packed cups) shredded coconut
9 oz. (1½ cups) semisweet chocolate chips, divided

steps: Adjust 2 racks to divide the oven into thirds.  Line cookie sheets with parchment paper.*
Sift together the flour, baking powder, and salt and set aside.
Place the butter in a small pan over low heat to melt.  Then set it aside to cool but do not let it harden—it must stay liquid.

Meanwhile, add the sugar to the eggs and beat at high speed for 5 minutes until the mixture is almost white.  On lowest speed add the sifted dry ingredients, scraping the bowl with a rubber spatula and beating only until incorporated.  Using a large rubber spatula, fold in the liquid butter and then the vanilla.  Then fold in the coconut, then ½ cup of the chocolate chips, and finally the cranberries.

Use a well-rounded teaspoonful of the mixture for each cookie and place them 1½ inches apart on the cookie sheets.  There should be 36 cookies.  Bake 2 sheets at a time, reversing the sheets top to bottom and front to back once during baking to insure even browning.*  Bake at 325° for 16 minutes or until some parts of the tops of the cookies are lightly golden-colored—some parts of the cookies will still be white.  With a wide metal spatula transfer the cookies to racks to cool.
Melt the remaining 1 cup of chocolate chips in the top of a small double boiler over warm water on low heat, stirring until completely smooth.  Turn off the stove.

Cover one or two cookie sheets with wax paper.  Dip the bottom of each cookie in the melted chocolate and smooth with a small spatula, making a thick layer.  After you spread the chocolate on a cookie, place it chocolate side down on the lined cookie sheet.  Refrigerate until the chocolate is firm and the cookies can be lifted easily.  Place them in an airtight box.  (Use wax paper between the layers.)  Store in the refrigerator.  Let them sit out a bit before serving.

title: Curry-Spiced Spinach
steps: Heat oil in a large skillet.  Add the coriander, curry powder, black pepper and raisins.  Stir to combine.  Cook for 10 seconds.  Add the spinach and salt.  Cook until most of the moisture evaporates.

title: Carbonara
steps: Remove the skin and any added seasonings from the guanciale. Cut into cubes. Ensure each piece has both meat and fat. Sauté over medium-high heat until fat is released and outside is crispy. Remove from heat. Reserve the fat and set the guanciale aside.

Cook pasta according to directions. Meanwhile, separate the eggs. Discard the whites (or save for another use) and place the yolks in a metal bowl (the bowl for a double-boiler is perfect). Add parmesan, pecorino and black pepper and whisk vigorously to form a paste. Add 2 tablespoons of guanciale fat and some hot pasta water (start with a half ladle or ⅛ cup).

To pasteurize the eggs, whisk vigorously over boiling water. As you stir over the heat, you should see the sauce become creamier. Be very careful not to get too close to the heat and never rest the sauce bowl on top of the pasta pot like a double boiler - you do not want to cook the eggs!

When the pasta is cooked al dente, add the guanciale and the pasta directly to the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce texture isn't quite right, add more grated cheese or pasta water. Plate and top with grated parmesan.

title: Chocolate Chip/Chunk Cookies
footnotes: It was difficult to incorporate chips into the dough.  After pressing some dough with chips in ¼-cup measure, I molded the dough and chips, put dough on cookie sheets, and then pressed additional chips into the dough.

ingredients.ingredient: 12 tablespoons (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, melted and cooled until warm
2 cups semi- or bittersweet chocolate chips or chunks

steps: Line cookie sheet with parchment paper.  Mix flour, salt, and baking soda in medium bowl.  Either by hand or mixer, mix butter and sugars in large bowl until thoroughly blend.
Mix in egg, egg yolk, and vanilla.  Mix in dry ingredients until just combined.  Stir in chips or chunks.*
Drop scant ¼ cup amounts of dough on cookie sheet. Leave plenty of room between cookie dough blobs.

Bake at 325°, reversing cookie sheet halfway through baking, until cookies are light golden brown and outer edges start to harden, but centers are still soft and puffy–15-18 minutes. Cool cookies on the cookie sheet. Makes about 20 cookies.

title: Carrot Loaf
footnotes: If you don’t have a food processor, everything may be done by hand (except beating the egg whites).
We always serve this on Rosh Hashanah, but it is delicious any time!
Can be fully prepared in advance without baking.
steps: Chop carrots finely in a food processor, using metal blade.  Add remaining ingredients except egg whites to processor and blend.  Pour into large bowl.

In a separate bowl, beat egg whites with an electric mixer until stiff and fold into carrot mixture.  Pour into greased loaf pan.  (If preparing in advance, cover and refrigerate.  Bring to room temperature before proceeding.)
Bake (uncovered) at 350° for 45 minutes.  Do not overbake; this should be very moist.  Remove from pan and serve warm as a side dish.

title: Chocolate Chip Pecan Pie

ingredients.ingredient: 2 oz. Crème de Cacao (or other liqueur, preferably with chocolate)

steps: Beat eggs slightly.  Add sugar gradually.  Add melted butter and Crème de Cacao; mix well.  Blend in cornstarch.  Add pecans and chocolate chips.  Pour into unbaked pie crust.  Bake at 350° for 45 – 50 minutes.  Cool 1 hour.
Can be made ahead.  Cover well with 2 layers of plastic and freeze.  To serve, thaw, keeping plastic on.  Remove plastic and reheat, uncovered, at 350° for 10 – 15 minutes.
To reheat frozen pie, heat, uncovered, at 350° for ~20 minutes.

title: Caviar Pastry Cups
source: Easy Gourmet-style Cooking with 5 Ingredients by Deborah Anderson

ingredients.ingredient: 15 frozen miniature phyllo dough pastry shells (pre-baked), thawed

steps: With a zester, grater, or knife, scrape off all of the yellow rind of the lemon without getting any of the white part.  Set aside.  Squeeze 2 tsp. of juice into small bowl.

Mix together the boursin cheese, lemon juice, and most of the scallions.  Fill each pastry shell with ½ tbsp. of the cheese mixture.  Top each with a dollop of caviar and a sprinkling of the remaining scallions.  Garnish with reserved lemon zest.

title: Bite-size Crab Quiches
source: Taste of Home Appetizers, Reader’s Digest

ingredients.ingredient: ½ lb. lump crabmeat, drained, flaked, and cartilage removed

ingredients.note: This was a lot of dough.  Some recipes call for 10¼ oz. tube.  The dough did not line the cups well, as it was a lot and it kept rising.  The quiches were mostly bread.  I would suggest either using less dough or trying a different type of dough, perhaps one that does not involve yeast.

steps: Separate biscuit dough into 24 equal pieces.  Press onto the bottom and up the sides of 24 ungreased miniature muffin cups.  Fill each cup with 2 tsp. crab and 1 tsp. Swiss cheese.  If making in advance, cover and refrigerate.
When you are ready to continue, combine the egg, milk, and dill.  Spoon about 1½ tsp. into each cup.
Bake at 375° for 15-20 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Let stand for 5 minutes before removing from pans.  Serve warm.

title: Crab Crescents
source: Taste of Home Appetizers, Reader’s Digest

ingredients.ingredient: 3 tbsp. prepared pesto (used fresh-made from DiBruno Brothers)

steps: Unroll crescent dough; separate into 8 triangles.  Cut each triangle in half lengthwise, forming 2 triangles.  Spread ½ teaspoon pesto over each triangle.  Place 1 rounded teaspoonful of crab along the wide end of each triangle.  Roll up triangles from the wide ends and place point side down 1 inch apart on an ungreased baking sheet.  Bake at 375° for 10 – 12 minutes or until golden brown.   Serve warm.

title: Cheesy Artichoke and Shrimp Bake
source: The Queen Victoria Cookbook by Anna Marie McMain

ingredients.note: Can substitute 2 egg whites for some whole eggs

steps: Combine eggs, flour, and baking powder in large bowl.  Stir in cheeses.  In skillet melt butter and lightly sauté onion and artichokes until artichoke hearts soften and crumble into pieces.  Remove from pan and cool.
Sauté shrimp in same pan; cool and cut into pieces.  Stir artichoke mixture and shrimp into egg and cheese mixture.
Pour into greased 9" x 13" baking dish.  Bake at 350° for 50 minutes until mixture is set and golden brown.  Let stand a few minutes before serving.
Can be prepared ahead, covered and refrigerated overnight.  Bring to room temperature before baking.

title: Dutch Baby

ingredients.note: Amounts in parentheses make a smaller pancake that serves 4.

steps: Place a 12" cast iron skillet in the center of the oven and preheat oven to 425°.  Whisk together the eggs, milk, flour, and sugar (and vanilla, if using) until very frothy.  You can use an electric mixer or blender.

Remove the skillet from the oven and melt the butter in it, tilting the pan until the butter coats the bottom and sides of the pan.  Pour the batter into the skillet.  Place the skillet into the center of the oven and bake for about 15 minutes until the pancake is golden brown and puffed up.  Carefully remove from pan (it will fall as it cools) and serve immediately.
_Serve with any of the following_
Maple syrup
Cinnamon sugar
Fresh fruit and/or berries
Lemon curd
Nutella
Powdered sugar
Honey
Whipped cream

title: Blintz Souffle
source: Breakfast at Nine Tea at Four, Favorite Recipes from the Mainstay Inn, Cape May, NJ by Sue Carroll

ingredients.ingredient: 1½ c. lowfat or nonfat sour cream
Lite cherry (or your favorite flavor) pie filling

steps: _Make the Filling:_ In a small bowl, cream cheese until smooth.  Add remaining filling ingredients and mix thoroughly.  Set aside.
In a separate bowl, cream margarine and sugar.  Add eggs and egg whites and beat well (a whisk helps).
In another bowl, mix flour and baking powder.  Add flour to egg mixture alternately with sour cream and orange juice.  Stir only until moistened.
Pour half of the batter into a buttered 9"x13" baking dish.  Spread filling over the batter.  The filling will be thick.
Cover with the remaining batter.  (If preparing in advance, cover and refrigerate.  Remove from the refrigerator 30 minutes before proceeding.)
Preheat oven to 350°.  Bake for 50 minutes.  Serve with warmed pie filling and additional sour cream or yogurt.

title: Cheese Nest Eggs
source: Annapolis Bed and Breakfast Association, Favorite Recipes, Volume 2; recipe from Peninsula House

ingredients.ingredient: 2 pounds Swiss or cheddar cheese, grated
Red pepper (used a little cayenne pepper)

steps: Butter a 3-quart casserole.  Line with cheese.  Make a well (the nest) in the cheese to hold each egg.  Break eggs into nests.
In a bowl mix whipping cream and mustard.  Spoon mixture over egg yolks until coated.  Sprinkle with salt and red pepper.
Bake at 325° for 20 minutes.  Watch carefully.  To serve, cut into "nests" and lift out.
Dish may be assembled and refrigerated the day before.  Bring to room temperature before baking.
I tried to make nest shapes, but the cheese spread out while baking.  However, it was easy to cut each "nest" and lift out of the dish.

title: Decadent Fudge Cookies

ingredients.ingredient: 14 oz. semi-sweet chocolate, cut in chunks
2 oz. unsweetened chocolate, cut in chunks
½ c. pecans, toasted and chopped
ingredients.note: Substituted white chocolate chips

ingredients.ingredient: ½ c. dried cherries, softened in water and patted dry
ingredients.note: Used dried cranberries

steps: Melt semi-sweet chocolate, unsweetened chocolate and butter in a double boiler over simmering water; set aside.
Beat eggs, white and brown sugars, and vanilla until light and fluffy.  (Used electric mixer.)
In a separate bowl, toss together the flour, baking soda, salt, pecans, chocolate chips, and dried fruit; set aside.
Pour melted chocolate mixture into egg/sugar mixture and combine thoroughly.  Stir in dry ingredients.  Set aside for a few minutes until mixture cools and batter is firm enough to scoop.

Line baking sheets with parchment.  Drop batter by teaspoonfuls onto sheets.  Bake at 375° for about 6 minutes—just until the tops begin to crack and the insides are still fudgy.  Cool on the baking sheets for 10 minutes, then transfer to rack.  When completely cool, store in airtight container.  Recipe says makes 3 dozen cookies.  Made 88 cookies

title: Espresso Brownies

ingredients.ingredient: 2 tbsp. instant espresso granules (decaf preferred) or instant decaf coffee, dissolved in 2 tbsp. hot water

steps: Stir together flour, baking powder, and salt in small bowl.

Put butter in large bowl and mix on medium speed for 15 seconds.  Add sugars and beat until butter and sugars are creamed thoroughly, about one minute.  Decrease speed to low and mix in eggs, dissolved espresso, and vanilla, mixing just until eggs are incorporated.  Mixture will look curdled.  Stop mixer and scrape sides of bowl once during mixing.  Slowly add flour mixture and mix just until flour is incorporated and mixture is smooth.  Stir in chips.

Spread evenly into greased 13" x 9" x 2" pan.  Bake at 325° until a toothpick inserted in center no longer has liquid clinging to it, but brownies still feel soft, 28 – 30 minutes.  Cool in pan thoroughly before cutting.

title: Easy Mulligatawny Soup
footnotes: If using pasta, add it to the soup when the remaining cooking time is equal to the amount of time the pasta needs to cook.
This would probably be main-course servings.  I omitted chicken, doubled recipe.  I served 11 appetizer portions, and had lots left over.  Single recipe probably makes about 8 appetizer portions.

ingredients.ingredient: 1 c. chopped apple (I used Granny Smith, peeled)
1 c. chopped carrot (I sliced baby carrots)
⅓ c. long grain rice (I used 1 cup Star of David-shaped pasta instead)
¼ tsp. coarsely ground black pepper
⅛ tsp. ground mace or nutmeg
1 tbsp. snipped fresh cilantro or parsley
1 14½-oz. can diced tomatoes, undrained (I used petite-cut)

steps: In a large saucepan (used 6-qt. for doubled recipe), combine broth, undrained tomatoes, apple, carrot, celery, rice*, onion, raisins, sugar, curry powder, pepper, and mace.  Bring to boiling; reduce heat.  Simmer, covered, about 20 minutes or until rice is tender.  Stir in chicken; heat through.  Stir in cilantro.  Makes about 8 cups, or 4 servings.*

title: Easy Baked Eggs

ingredients.ingredient: 12 eggs (substituted 6 whole eggs and 12 egg whites)
3 c. shredded cheese (Cheddar, Swiss, Jarlsberg, Monterey Jack, or a blend)—I use 2 c. Swiss and 1 c. sharp Cheddar

steps: Melt butter in a small skillet over medium-low heat.  Sauté onions, mushrooms, and shrimp, if using, until soft.  Cut shrimp into bite-sized pieces.

In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs (can use electric mixer).  Add all other ingredients except ½ cup of the cheese.  Pour into a greased ovenproof 2-quart casserole.  (I use 7" x 11" Pyrex baking dish.)

Bake uncovered at 350° for 30 minutes or until mixture is set.  Remove from oven and sprinkle with remaining cheese.  (Use extra cheese, if needed, to lightly cover entire top.)  Continue to bake until cheese melts.
Halves well.
Can substitute any of the following for the shrimp:
—1½ cups. crumbled cooked bacon (~14-16 strips)
—½ lb. Canadian bacon, cooked and  cut into bite-sized pieces
—3 oz. Nova Scotia smoked salmon, cut into bite-sized pieces
Can also add halved grape tomatoes, to your taste

title: Fudgy Chocolate Chip Cookies
steps: In heavy saucepan, melt 1 cup chocolate chips with butter, stirring constantly.  Cool slightly.

Beat egg with sugars and vanilla until creamed.  Mix in melted chocolate.  Stir flour with baking soda, baking powder and salt.  Combine milk with lemon juice, stirring until thick.  Add dry ingredients to chocolate mixture alternately with milk.  Stir in remaining cup chocolate chips and cranberries.  Chill dough.
Drop by tablespoon onto ungreased baking sheet.  Bake at 350° for 8 – 10 minutes.  (I did 8 minutes.)  Cool on rack.  Makes about 5 dozen cookies.
Freezes well.

title: Fudge Pie

ingredients.ingredient: 1 10" pie crust, unbaked and frozen in pie pan (used deep-dish 9" crust)
½ cup whipping cream, at room temperature
Whipped cream, for serving with the pie

steps: Bake pie crust according to package directions.  Cool.

Put the semisweet chocolate, unsweetened chocolate, and butter in the top of a double boiler over barely simmering water.  Stir together until melted.  Remove from over the water and set aside to cool slightly.

Put the eggs in a large bowl and mix on low speed just to blend the yolks and whites together.  Add the sugar, coffee, vanilla, and rum and beat for 2 minutes.  Add the chocolate mixture and beat just until the chocolate and eggs are mixed together completely.  Mix in the whipping cream.

Slowly pour the filling into the pie crust.  The filling will come up to the top of the pie crust.  Bake at 350° for 35 minutes.  The pie will look crackly on the top and feel soft, but it will firm as it cools.  (If using deep-dish 9" crust, may need to bake a few more minutes.)  Cool thoroughly.

To freeze for later use, wrap tightly with plastic wrap, then heavy aluminum foil.  To serve, defrost the covered pie at room temperature or in the refrigerator for 6 hours.  Serve at room temperature or chilled.  The chocolate will have a more intense taste at room temp.  Serve with whipped cream.  Store leftover pie in the frig.

title: Fudge Nut Crumb Bars
steps: Beat butter in large bowl until creamy.  Beat in flour, sugar, and salt until crumbly.  (Used pastry blender to help.)  With floured fingers, press 2 cups crumb mixture into bottom of greased 13" x 9" baking pan; reserve remaining mixture.  Bake at 350° for 10-12 minutes or until edges are golden brown.
Meanwhile, warm 1½ cups chocolate chips and sweetened condensed milk in small, heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.  Stir in vanilla.  Spread over hot crust.

Stir nuts and remaining chocolate chips into reserved crumb mixture; sprinkle over fudge filling.  Bake at 350° for 25-30 minutes or until center is set.  Cool in pan on wire rack; cut into squares.  Makes ~30 squares.

title: Fruited Spinach Salad with Currant Vinaigrette

ingredients.ingredient: 8 cups cleaned spinach leaves, stems removed (or baby spinach or other greens)

steps: For the vinaigrette, in a small saucepan combine currant jelly and vinegar.  Cook and stir over medium-low heat just till jelly melts and mixture is smooth.  Chill in the freezer for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, in a large salad bowl combine spinach, strawberries, orange sections, and green onion.  Drizzle vinaigrette over the spinach mixture; toss to mix.  Sprinkle with almonds and cheese and toss gently.  Serve immediately.  Serves 6-8.

title: Fruited Rice Combo

ingredients.ingredient: ½ c. basmati rice (I used brown basmati)
½ c. dried cherries or cranberries (I used cherries)

steps: Bring water to boil in saucepan and add wild rice.  Stir, cover, and simmer about 35 minutes or until just tender (took longer—check package instructions).  Drain excess liquid and transfer to large bowl.

Boil pineapple juice in 2nd saucepan and add basmati rice.  Stir, cover, and simmer 20 minutes (took much longer—check package instructions).  Liquid should be totally absorbed and rice tender.  Add to wild rice.
Heat oil in skillet and sauté onions, garlic, and mushrooms until soft.  Combine with rice mixture.  (Stop here if preparing in advance.)
Stir in remaining ingredients.  Transfer to greased 8" square baking pan.  Cover and bake for 30 minutes at 350°.

title: Forest Mushroom Pastry Cups

ingredients.ingredient: 1 (2.1-ounce) package frozen mini filo dough shells
3 ounces fresh shiitake mushrooms, finely chopped
2 ounces Monterey Jack Cheese, cut into 15 (½-inch) cubes
ingredients.note: You might want to halve this amount.

ingredients.ingredient: 1½ ounces (⅓ cup) Monterey Jack Cheese, shredded

steps: Heat oven to 350°F. Place shells onto ungreased baking sheet.  Combine mushrooms and hoisin sauce in small bowl.  Place 1 cube cheese in each shell.  Spoon mushroom mixture evenly into shells; sprinkle with shredded cheese.  Bake for 5 to 8 minutes or until heated through.  Remove immediately.  Serve warm.

TIP: To make ahead, prepare as directed except do not bake.  Layer between sheets of waxed paper in a resealable plastic freezer container; freeze.  At serving time, heat oven to 350°F. Place desired number of pastry cups onto ungreased baking sheet.  Bake for 12 to 20 minutes or until filling is hot.  Serve warm.

title: Flourless Chocolate Chocolate Chip Cookies
footnotes: Can dust with powdered sugar when still slightly warm.

ingredients.ingredient: 3 tbsp. butter, room temperature and cut into a few pieces
⅓ c. sugar, plus more for rolling

steps: Melt chocolate in top of double boiler.  Remove from heat and mix in butter until melted.
Beat eggs with electric mixer.  Gradually add sugar until ribbons form.  Fold in the chocolate mixture.  Gently add the almonds.  Fold in chips.  Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Heat oven to 325°.  Line baking sheet with parchment.
Form the dough into 1" balls.  Roll in granulated sugar and place on sheet 2" apart.  Bake 10-12 minutes until centers are no longer wet and cookies are puffed and cracked.*

title: Flourless Chocolate Cake

ingredients.ingredient: 1 cup (2 sticks) butter, cut into pieces

ingredients.note: If making for passover, use Kosher for Passover products for ingredients marked KP

steps: _For the Cake:_

Butter a 10" diameter springform pan.  Line bottom with waxed paper.  Stir butter and chocolate in heavy large saucepan over low heat until melted.  Mix sugar and cocoa in large bowl.  Add eggs; whisk until well blended.  Whisk in chocolate-butter mixture.  Pour batter into prepared pan.  Bake at 350° until tester inserted into center comes out clean, about 40-45 minutes.
